implementation.name: GNU C++ compiler with libstdc++

sources.label: GCC compilation stages and C/C++ invocation
libstdc++ license and runtime exception scope
C++ Core Guidelines: resource management and RAII

fit.text: Native applications using C++ and its standard library; platform and linked-library choices remain explicit.

prerequisites.text: Learn compilation and object lifetimes together; raw pointers, owning handles and library resources need explicit distinctions.

execution.text: Invoke g++ for C++ source so the expected C++ library linkage is supplied.

behavior.text: Constructors and destructors support resource lifetime management. The Core Guidelines recommend RAII handles and explicit ownership instead of manual cleanup paths.

tooling.text: g++ accepts source files and options; separate object generation and final linking when builds grow.

maintenance.text: Choose a target compiler and compatible standard library together; inspect the notices shipped with that combination.

costs.text: libstdc++ has a scoped runtime exception. Conditions depend on eligible compilation and the covered files.

implementation.name: C3 compiler (c3c)
implementation.version_scope: The documented native compiler and current tutorial syntax; no binary has been executed for this profile.

sources.label: C3 compiler targets and application scope

fit.text: C3 targets native applications, libraries and systems software, including games and command-line tools.

prerequisites.text: The tutorial assumes an installed c3c compiler and introduces modules, fn declarations and the standard I/O module.

execution.text: Compile a .c3 source to an executable, or use compile-run for the same local workflow.

behavior.text: Module imports make library names available; printn writes a value followed by a newline.

tooling.text: The project publishes Windows, macOS and Linux compiler packages; the tutorial provides a direct CLI starting point.

maintenance.text: Keep the compiler and its standard-library documentation together when reproducing an example.

costs.text: The compiler carries MIT terms; retain its copyright and licence when redistributing the implementation.

example.run_instructions: With c3c installed, run c3c compile-run hello.c3. Alternatively run c3c compile hello.c3 and launch the generated executable.

implementation.name: CLIPS 6.4 rule engine
implementation.version_scope: CLIPS 6.4 syntax and the publisher's v6.4.2 user-guide distribution.

sources.label: CLIPS 6.4 rules, facts and console commands

fit.text: Model heuristic expert-system decisions with facts and rules; the publisher also provides procedural and object facilities.

prerequisites.text: Learn asserted facts, rule conditions and the agenda before adding rule priorities.

execution.text: Load constructs into the engine, assert facts and run the agenda to fire matching rules.

behavior.text: A rule's actions run when its conditions match facts; priority and reactivation affect which actions execute.

tooling.text: CLIPS provides a portable C implementation and documentation for embedding the engine in host applications.

maintenance.text: Resetting facts and agenda state is part of reproducing a rule session; saved constructs and saved facts are distinct.

costs.text: The publisher declares CLIPS public-domain software. This declaration has not been mapped to an SPDX dedication licence.

example.run_instructions: In the CLIPS console, enter (load "decision.clp"), then (reset), (assert (choice approved)) and (run).
example.expected_result: The asserted fact activates the rule, which prints PLLDN.

licenses.scope: Named implementation only; dependencies and generated applications require separate review.
licenses.notice: The publisher declares public-domain status, but an exact SPDX dedication instrument was not established; do not substitute Unlicense or CC0.

execution.text: cmake -P executes a script without creating a build system; script mode cannot define build targets.

behavior.text: Command arguments expand variables and lists; quoted arguments preserve a single argument's structure.

prerequisites.text: Learn COBOL divisions and source-format rules; free-format compilation is selected explicitly in this example.

execution.text: cobc -x builds an executable; COBOL modules and calls can instead use the libcob runtime.

behavior.text: CALL behavior and module loading depend on compiler options and runtime configuration.

tooling.text: The project documents source-level debugging and native targets on Windows, macOS and Unix-like platforms.

implementation.name: Cairo local executable through Scarb
implementation.version_scope: The Cairo book's local executable workflow with matching Scarb and cairo_execute versions; this is not a deployed contract.

fit.text: Cairo expresses provable computations; Starknet contracts are one application, while local programs have a separate workflow.

prerequisites.text: Install Scarb and match the executable dependency to its Cairo version; the tutorial also introduces the project manifest.

execution.text: Scarb builds an executable target and executes its annotated entry function locally.

behavior.text: An executable function uses #[executable]; println! is a macro and statements end with semicolons.

tooling.text: Scarb provides project creation, build, execution and formatting; source modules reside beneath src.

maintenance.text: Keep the edition, executable target and cairo_execute dependency consistent with the selected Scarb toolchain.

costs.text: The Cairo compiler is Apache-2.0; Scarb packages and contract deployment have separate components and terms.

example.run_instructions: Place hello_world.cairo at src/hello_world.cairo in the documented project layout. Create a hello_world project with scarb new hello_world. Use the linked tutorial's local-executable Scarb.toml, including cairo_execute matching the selected toolchain and function hello_world::hello_world::main. Set src/lib.cairo to mod hello_world; and save this file. From the project directory run scarb build, then scarb execute.
example.expected_result: The local executable prints PLLDN; this workflow does not deploy a contract or produce an on-chain transaction.

licenses.scope: Cairo compiler repository; Scarb and additional packages are separate.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

implementation.name: Circom 2 Rust compiler
implementation.version_scope: Circom 2 circuit syntax; constraint compilation is separate from witness generation and proving.

sources.label: Circom circuit/compiler scope and Circom 1 deprecation
Circom constraints, witness targets and inspection options

fit.text: Describe arithmetic circuits for zero-knowledge workflows; proving systems are provided by separate tools.

prerequisites.text: Learn signals and constraints, then install the Circom 2 compiler; a conventional assignment is not automatically a constraint.

execution.text: Compilation produces R1CS constraints and optionally WebAssembly or C++ witness-generation code.

behavior.text: <== both assigns a signal expression and adds its constraint; the top-level main component instantiates a circuit.

tooling.text: Compiler options produce symbols and inspection checks; the project links syntax highlighters and circuit-analysis tools.

maintenance.text: The JavaScript Circom 1 compiler is deprecated; distinguish its syntax and tooling from Circom 2.

costs.text: The distribution contains GPLv3 COPYING text; generated circuits and proving-tool packages require their own licence review.

example.run_instructions: With Circom 2 installed, run circom sum.circom --r1cs --wasm --sym. Witness generation and proof generation are subsequent steps documented separately.
example.expected_result: The compiler produces sum.r1cs, sum.sym and the WebAssembly witness-generator directory. The circuit constrains total to left + right.

licenses.notice: COPYING supplies GPLv3 text, but a component-level grant establishing only-versus-or-later was not confirmed. Do not apply compiler terms automatically to generated circuits.
